deploy-bot: [1865432100] Deploy queued: repo=redwood/runtime tag=v2.7.1 env=prod reason=concurrency_limit reached. Queue position 3/5. Estimated start ~8m. To cancel: `/deploy cancel 1234`. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jess: Thanks — any chance to bump priority? This is a critical hotfix for payments.
ryan: What's blocking? Do we have any long-running deploys we can pause or evict?
infra-bot: Current active deploys: 2 (ids: 1229, 1230). Max concurrent = 2 for prod-ephemeral pool. Eviction not allowed for prod without release-owner approval.
anya: If it's payments hotfix I can approve an eviction for one job. Which job is safest to evict?
deploy-bot: Queue snapshot: position 3. Active deploy 1229 (release-owner: olivia, tag v2.7.0-metrics) started 6m ago. Active deploy 1230 (release-owner: paul) started 1m ago.
olivia: I'm mid-canary for v2.7.0-metrics — can't evict. Paul is currently on PTO. @paul FYI.
ryan: Paul is OOO, ok. Alternative: can we retarget the hotfix to the reserved-hotfix pool if there is capacity? That avoids evicting.
jess: We can do that — how do we change the target pool without re-running CI?
deploy-bot: To re-target: use:
```
deploy promote --id 1234 --pool reserved-hotfix
```
Pool has 1 free slot. Note: reserved pools require entitlement `hotfix-promo`.
anya: I can grant `hotfix-promo` to jess, doing that now.
infra-bot: Entitlement granted to jess. reserved-hotfix free slots: 1.
jess: Promoting now.
deploy-bot: Promotion accepted. New assignment: deploy 1234 -> reserved-hotfix. Starting in ~20s. Commit: 8a1f3df tag=v2.7.1-hotfix.
ryan: Great. If it fails, what's the rollback plan? Should we pin traffic back to previous stable?
jess: Canary 10% for 5m. Auto-rollback on errors >1% or latency spike above threshold. Manual rollback command if needed:
```
deploy rollback --release v2.7.0
```
olivia: Heads up to oncall for observability: @oncall please watch payments success rate and p95 latency during canary.
infra-bot: Deploy 1234 started on reserved-hotfix. Steps: pulling image -> warmup -> starting instances.
deploy-bot: Deploy 1234 finished successfully. Duration 75s. Canary 10% live. :tada:
ryan: I'll keep an eye on dashboards for the next 10m.
jess: I'll post a quick release note and add the changelog entry after canary. Thanks all!
